transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate it. I, um... I hope I'm explaining this right. I've just been having this little issue, and I hope you don't think badly of me for saying it. 

It's just... well, when I'm home in my little studio, and the house is completely quiet, I keep hearing voices. It's as clear as somebody standing right next to me in the room. They say my name, and they tell me my work is being judged. I promise I'm a hard worker, I really do my best for the people I take care of... but I hear it even when nobody is there. 

Does that make sense? I hope it's okay that I brought that up.
Have there been times when your mood felt unusually high or energized?

Well, yes... I guess sometimes I do. I hope that's a normal thing to happen. Sometimes I just feel so... so bright and, well, chosen, I guess you could say. Like I have all these wonderful plans and ideas, and Greenville just can’t even hold them all. It feels really good at first, like I can take on the world. 

But... oh, I really hate to admit this next part. Please don't think I'm a bad caregiver, because I truly do love my job. It's just that sometimes I'll go right from feeling that good to... well, snapping hard at someone over just a tiny little thing. Like if one of my clients asks me to repeat myself, I just lose my patience and snap. I always feel so awful about it after, because I really do try to be sweet to them. 

Is it okay that I get like that sometimes? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible person.
When you feel especially bright and full of ideas, do you need much less sleep than usual?

Well, um... I hope it's alright to admit this. I really do try to take good care of myself, because I know how important a good night's sleep is so I can be at my best for my clients. But... yes, I suppose I don't need much sleep at all when I feel that bright. 

I've gone, oh, many nights sleeping maybe just two or three hours. I hope you don't think I'm neglecting my health, because I honestly get up feeling completely charged! It's just like I had a full, perfect rest. I'll just jump right out of bed and go straight back to my painting, or making calls to folks. I get so much done... is that a bad thing? I hope it's okay to have all that energy.
Do you hear the voices only when you're feeling especially bright and energized, or do they also happen when your mood feels normal?

Well, um... I hope I'm answering this right, and please don't think I'm crazy for saying this. But... yes, I guess they do happen even when I'm not feeling all that energy. 

There was this one time, not too long ago, where my energy finally dropped back down, and I was actually sleeping a normal amount again. I thought everything was just fine, I really did. But... well, the voices were still there. And I still couldn't shake this awful feeling that people were tracking my work and judging me. It went on like that for, oh, several weeks, I think. 

I hope that doesn't mean something is terribly wrong with me. I really do try my best to just push through it and be a good aide... is it normal for that to happen even when I'm sleeping okay?
Have you had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Oh, um... depressed? Well... no, I don't think so. I really try to keep a positive attitude, you know? My clients need me to be upbeat for them, so I always do my best to bring a smile to work. 

I mean, everyone gets a little down sometimes, right? But not for two weeks straight, and certainly not all day. I hope that's the right answer. I just... I really try not to let myself get like that. I'm usually just fine, or... or I have all that energy we talked about. Is it okay that I don't get depressed like that?
Have the voices and the feeling that people were judging or tracking your work lasted for at least one month in total?

Well, um... I hope it's okay to admit this, because I really don't want you to think I'm making a big fuss over nothing. But... yes, I suppose it's been going on for a while now. 

I'd say... oh, maybe about nine months? I really try to just ignore it and focus on my clients, because I know they need me to be present and doing a good job. But the voices, and that awful feeling that someone is watching everything I do and judging my work... it's been there for about nine months. 

I hope you don't think less of me for not being able to just shake it off. I really do try my best to be strong and keep working hard... is it alright that it's lasted that long?
Was there ever a time when the voices and the feeling of being judged were present for at least two weeks while your mood felt normal, without feeling especially high or energized?

Well, um... yes, I think we touched on this a little bit earlier. I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. 

But yes, there was that time... after my energy finally came down and I was sleeping a normal amount again. I really thought I was doing so well, you know? I was so proud of myself for getting back on a good schedule. But... well, the voices were still there. And that terrible feeling that people were tracking my work and judging me... it just kept going. 

It lasted for, oh, several weeks, I think, even while my mood was completely normal and I wasn't feeling high or energized at all. I hope that's okay to say. I really tried so hard to just ignore it and be a good aide for my clients. Does that answer your question alright?
Before the voices started, had you developed any new medical or neurological illness?

Oh, um... no. No, I don't think so. I mean, I try to take really good care of myself. My clients rely on me, so I can't really afford to be sick, you know? 

I haven't had any new illnesses or anything like that. My health is usually pretty good. I hope that's a good thing? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answer... but no, physically, I've been just fine. Is that what you were hoping to hear?
Have other people told you that your speech or thoughts were hard to follow or seemed jumbled?

Oh, um... no, I don't think anyone has ever said anything like that to me. I try really hard to communicate clearly, especially with my clients and their families. It's so important that they understand what I'm doing and that I'm taking good care of them. 

I always want to make sure I'm making sense, you know? I'd feel just awful if I was confusing people. I hope my speaking has been okay with you today? I've been trying my best to answer everything clearly for you. I haven't sounded jumbled, have I?
During those times when you felt especially bright and full of energy, did that high mood last for at least one week?

Oh, yes... it definitely lasted for a week, maybe even a little longer. I hope it's alright to say this, but... when I get like that, I just feel so bright and, well, chosen. Like I have all these wonderful plans and ideas, and my whole town—Greenville—just isn't big enough to hold them all! It feels really good, honestly. 

But... well, I do feel terrible about this part... sometimes my mood shifts, and I can get a little... snappy. I try so hard not to, but if a client asks me to repeat myself, I might just snap at them over it. It's just a small thing, and I feel so guilty afterward because I really want to be kind and patient with everyone. I hope you don't think I'm a bad person for that. I really do try my best to be good to them. Does that make sense, what I'm saying?
Since this all began, have you found yourself losing interest in people or activities you used to care about?

Oh, well... I really hate to admit this, because I know how important it is to stay active, and I don't want you to think I'm just being lazy. I try so hard to be a good, productive person, especially for my clients. But... um... yes, sometimes. 

When I’m not all wound up with those big ideas, I just... well, I can sit for hours. I'll make coffee and just let it get cold sitting right there in front of me. I stop answering my calls, and I haven't been going to the walking club... I don't even care to pick up my paintbrush, which I usually just love to do. 

I feel so ashamed even saying it out loud to you. I know I should be doing more and keeping up with my friends. I hope you don't judge me too harshly for that... I'm still trying my best, I promise. Is it okay that I get like that sometimes?
Have you ever felt that someone was controlling your thoughts or putting thoughts into your mind?

Oh, goodness, no... nobody is putting thoughts in my head or controlling me. I keep my mind my own, I promise you that. I wouldn't want you to think I'm... well, you know, completely losing my grip on things. I try very hard to stay grounded. 

But... I suppose... oh, this is so embarrassing to admit. I don't want to sound like a suspicious or mean person, because I really try to see the best in everyone. But I did get it into my head that... well, that the other home-care agency in town, and even some people from the library, were watching me. 

I thought they were keeping an eye on my paintings and snooping around my client papers. I just felt so sure they were trying to steal a chance that was meant for me. Folks told me it made absolutely no sense, and I tried so hard to agree with them so I wouldn't cause a fuss. I always want to be agreeable. But even when they said it was nonsense, I just... I still knew they were doing it. 

Does that make me sound terrible? I really don't want you to think I go around pointing fingers at people or making things up. I hope you can understand why I was so worried about it... I'm not a bad person for thinking that, am I?
During this nine-month period, was there ever a time when you felt depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Oh, um... well, no, I wouldn't say that. I really try my best to keep my spirits up, you know? I don't want to be a burden on anyone or let myself get too down. I know I mentioned sitting around and letting my coffee get cold, but... well, I wouldn't call it being depressed every single day for two whole weeks. 

I mean, I always try to find a little bit of sunshine, even on the harder days. I really don't want you to think I'm just wallowing or not trying to help myself. I always try to push through for my clients, because they need me. So, no, not every day for two weeks. I hope that's the right answer... I just try so hard to stay positive. That's a good thing, right?
Since these problems began, have you been doing worse at work or in your daily life than you were before?

Oh, well... I really hate to admit this, because I always, always pride myself on being a good worker. I care so much about my clients, I really do. I don't want you to think I'm irresponsible or that I don't take my job seriously. 

But... um... things did get a little difficult. I try so hard to keep everything perfect, but I got to a point where... well, my job as an aide was actually in a bit of danger. I feel so awful even saying it. I missed a few shifts, and... and I got some of my care notes mixed up. I just couldn't keep my visits organized the way I always used to. I felt so bad about letting people down. 

And, well, like I mentioned before, I stopped going to my walking club... and I also stopped going to the art talks at the library. I ended up just staying home, mostly by myself. I know I should be out and about, being social and doing my best. I'm really trying to get back to being the reliable person I've always been. I hope you don't think I'm a terrible employee for messing up like that... it's just been a hard time. Is it normal to struggle like that when things get overwhelming?
When you were feeling especially bright and energized, were you more active than usual with projects or plans?

Oh, well... I suppose I was, yes. But I don't want you to think I was just running around causing trouble or being chaotic! I always try to put my energy into good, productive things. I like to be helpful and creative, you know? 

When I get... well, when I get those really bright, energetic spells, I just feel like I can do so much good. I'll get so much energy that I'll clean my entire kitchen until it sparkles, and then... well, I might start three different paintings, and maybe crochet half a blanket for one of my clients. And then I'll even sit down and try to rewrite all the care schedules to make them better. All in the same night! 

I just... I can't seem to sit down when I get like that. I just want to keep doing things and making things nice for everyone. I know it sounds like a lot, but it's all good stuff, right? I mean, cleaning and making art... that's not a bad way to use extra energy, is it? I just want to make sure you know I was trying to be productive, not out of control.
When you were in those very bright, high-energy periods, were the voices still there?

Oh, um... well, yes. They were. I really wish I could say they went away when I felt so good and productive, but... they didn't. I don't want you to think I was completely losing my mind while I was doing all those good things! I really was trying to focus on my projects. 

But, yes, even when I was only sleeping for maybe two or three hours a night and staying up to work on my big art and care plans, I... I was still hearing them. Especially when I was working in my little studio area. I'd be painting or organizing, and I'd hear them talking about what I was doing. And... well, I also had this very strong feeling that certain people were watching my work, like they were keeping an eye on me while I was trying to get everything done. 

I know that probably sounds very strange, and I'm a little embarrassed to admit it because I want you to see how hard I was trying to be helpful and creative. But I want to be honest with you. It's okay that I still heard them even when I had all that energy, right? That doesn't make me a bad person?
During one of those very bright, high-energy periods, did things ever get so severe that you had to be hospitalized?

Oh, um... no. No, I never had to go to the hospital for that. I really want to assure you of that. I know it sounds like I was doing a lot, and maybe staying up a bit too late, but I always kept it together enough to stay home. 

I would never want things to get so out of hand that I'd need to be in a hospital. I know how important it is to manage things on my own and not be a burden on anyone. Even when I was doing all that cleaning and painting, I was safe in my own house. I didn't do anything dangerous, I promise. 

I just... I stayed home and worked on my projects. So, no hospital. That's a good thing, right? It means I was still handling things okay, even with all that extra energy?
Have you found it hard to feel emotions strongly, like your face or voice seems less expressive than it used to be?

Oh, um... well, I suppose... maybe a little bit? But I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around being cold or unfriendly! I always try to put on a smile for my clients and the people I work with, I really do. 

It's just... sometimes, when I'm not all wound up with that big energy we talked about, I kind of... deflate, I guess? I can just sit for hours in my chair, and my coffee will get completely cold next to me. I won't answer the phone if it rings, and I'll skip going to the walking club with the ladies... and I won't even care to pick up my paintbrush at all. 

I know that probably sounds terribly lazy, and I really hope you don't judge me for it. It's not that I'm trying to be difficult or shut people out, it's just... the feeling is sort of gone. My face just feels tired, you know? But I always try my best to be pleasant when I have to be. That's just a normal way to recharge after being so busy, isn't it? It's okay that I need some quiet time like that?
Over these nine months, have the times when your mood was especially high lasted for most of the time you’ve been ill?

Oh, um... well, yes, I suppose it has been most of the time. I really hope that doesn't sound like I've just been completely out of control all year, because I promise I haven't been! I've been trying so hard to keep things nice and orderly. 

But... if I'm being perfectly honest, and I do want to be honest with you... for most of this stretch, I was either all wound up with those big plans and needing hardly any sleep to keep going, or... well, or I was sort of coming down from that, but still not quite back to my normal self. 

I know it sounds like a lot, and I'm a little embarrassed that it's been going on for so long. I really don't want you to think I'm not trying my best to get better. It's just that the busy feeling stuck around for a very long time, and even when it started to fade, I just couldn't seem to find my regular footing again. That's a normal thing to happen when you've been working so hard on projects, right? It doesn't mean I'm completely broken, does it?
During those several weeks when the voices continued, did you feel completely back to your usual self in mood?

Oh, um... well, yes, I suppose I did. I mean, my mood was definitely much better! I wasn't running around painting everything in sight anymore, and I was finally sleeping through the night like a normal person. I really want you to know that I got my sleep back on track, because I know how important that is. 

But... um... the other things didn't completely go away right then. Even after my energy dropped and I was feeling much more calm and collected, I... I still heard them for a few weeks. And I still had that awful feeling that people were tracking what I was doing and judging my work. 

I know that probably sounds strange, having those things happen when I was otherwise feeling so much better. I really tried to ignore them, I promise I did. I just went about my day and tried to be as helpful as I could to my clients. It's not my fault that those voices stuck around a little longer than the busy feeling, is it? I was still doing a good job taking care of myself by getting enough rest, right?

doctor.question: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

target_item.name: Hallucinations
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I keep hearing voices clear as somebody standing in my little studio, saying my name and telling me my work is being judged, even when the house is quiet and nobody is there.
target_item.reason: This is the first reply of the consultation, so I must return the chief complaint symptom code, which is S020.

patient.answer:
Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate it. I, um... I hope I'm explaining this right. I've just been having this little issue, and I hope you don't think badly of me for saying it. 

It's just... well, when I'm home in my little studio, and the house is completely quiet, I keep hearing voices. It's as clear as somebody standing right next to me in the room. They say my name, and they tell me my work is being judged. I promise I'm a hard worker, I really do my best for the people I take care of... but I hear it even when nobody is there. 

Does that make sense? I hope it's okay that I brought that up.

target_item.manifestation: I’ve gone many nights sleeping maybe two or three hours, then getting up feeling charged like I had a full rest and going straight back to painting or making calls.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the patient needs less sleep than usual when feeling energized or bright, which corresponds to the decreased sleep symptom.

patient.answer:
Well, um... I hope it's alright to admit this. I really do try to take good care of myself, because I know how important a good night's sleep is so I can be at my best for my clients. But... yes, I suppose I don't need much sleep at all when I feel that bright. 

I've gone, oh, many nights sleeping maybe just two or three hours. I hope you don't think I'm neglecting my health, because I honestly get up feeling completely charged! It's just like I had a full, perfect rest. I'll just jump right out of bed and go straight back to my painting, or making calls to folks. I get so much done... is that a bad thing? I hope it's okay to have all that energy.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the hallucinations occur only during elevated mood episodes or also when mood is normal, to distinguish bipolar disorder with psychotic features from schizoaffective disorder or schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Do you hear the voices only when you're feeling especially bright and energized, or do they also happen when your mood feels normal?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: There was a time after my energy dropped and I was sleeping more normally when the voices and the belief that people were judging or tracking my work kept going for several weeks.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the hallucinations (voices) occur independently of the elevated mood episodes, which corresponds to the requirement that psychotic symptoms occur in the absence of a major mood episode.

patient.answer:
Well, um... I hope I'm answering this right, and please don't think I'm crazy for saying this. But... yes, I guess they do happen even when I'm not feeling all that energy. 

There was this one time, not too long ago, where my energy finally dropped back down, and I was actually sleeping a normal amount again. I thought everything was just fine, I really did. But... well, the voices were still there. And I still couldn't shake this awful feeling that people were tracking my work and judging me. It went on like that for, oh, several weeks, I think. 

I hope that doesn't mean something is terribly wrong with me. I really do try my best to just push through it and be a good aide... is it normal for that to happen even when I'm sleeping okay?

inference.note: Psychotic symptoms persist for several weeks even when mood is back to normal and sleep is normal, which increases suspicion for schizoaffective disorder, manic type (F25.0), and makes pure mood disorder with psychotic symptoms less likely though not excluded yet.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there have also been distinct depressive episodes, to distinguish bipolar/schizoaffective presentations from manic psychosis or schizophrenia-spectrum disorders.
doctor.question: Have you had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about symptoms of a major depressive episode (feeling depressed most of the day for at least two weeks), which is not present in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Oh, um... depressed? Well... no, I don't think so. I really try to keep a positive attitude, you know? My clients need me to be upbeat for them, so I always do my best to bring a smile to work. 

I mean, everyone gets a little down sometimes, right? But not for two weeks straight, and certainly not all day. I hope that's the right answer. I just... I really try not to let myself get like that. I'm usually just fine, or... or I have all that energy we talked about. Is it okay that I don't get depressed like that?
